record.original_question: If a Banach algebra A is approximately amenable, meaning that every continuous derivation from A into the dual of any Banach A-bimodule is approximately inner, must A have a two-sided approximate identity, and must it even have a bounded approximate identity?

evidence.quote: Definition 1.2. A Banach algebra A is called (resp. boundedly, sequentially, uniformly or weak* ) approximately amenable if every continuous derivation D: A -> X* is (resp. boundedly, sequentially, uniformly or weak* ) approximately inner for each Banach A-bimodule X.
Theorem 3.3. Let A be a Banach algebra. (1) If A is approximately amenable, then it has a left and a right approximate identities [14].
Question 4. Does every approximately amenable Banach algebra have a two-sided approximate identity? Does it have a bounded approximate identity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a Banach algebra. A continuous linear map D: A → X from A into a Banach A-bimodule X is called a derivation if D(ab) = a·D(b) + D(a)·b for all a,b ∈ A. For x ∈ X, the inner derivation ad_x: A → X is defined by ad_x(a) = a·x − x·a. The derivation D is said to be approximately inner if there exists a net (x_α) in X such that D(a) = lim_α ad_{x_α}(a) for every a ∈ A, with the limit taken in the norm topology of X.

The Banach algebra A is called approximately amenable if, for every Banach A-bimodule X, every continuous derivation D: A → X* (where X* is the dual A-bimodule of X) is approximately inner.

A net (e_α) in A is called a left (resp. right) approximate identity if e_α a → a (resp. a e_α → a) in norm for every a ∈ A. It is a two-sided approximate identity if it is both a left and a right approximate identity. It is bounded if sup_α ‖e_α‖ < ∞.

It is known that every approximately amenable Banach algebra has a left approximate identity and a right approximate identity. Decide the following:

(a) Must every approximately amenable Banach algebra possess a two-sided approximate identity?

(b) Must every approximately amenable Banach algebra possess a bounded approximate identity?
artifact.status_search_result: Part (b) was answered negatively by F. Ghahramani and C. J. Read (2012, "Approximate identities in approximate amenability", J. Funct. Anal.), who constructed Banach algebras that are even boundedly approximately amenable but do not possess any bounded approximate identity. Part (a), regarding the existence of a two-sided (not necessarily bounded) approximate identity in every approximately amenable Banach algebra, does not appear to have been resolved in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Approximate identities in approximate amenability
status_evidence.snippet: Examples of Banach algebras which are boundedly approximately amenable but do not have bounded approximate identities, answering a question open since 2000.
status_evidence.claim: Ghahramani and Read constructed boundedly approximately amenable Banach algebras without bounded approximate identities, settling part (b) negatively.
